newsitem.title: UK: U.S. entrepreneur eyeing Laura Ashley -paper.
newsitem.headline: U.S. entrepreneur eyeing Laura Ashley -paper.

text.p: U.S. cosmetics entrepreneur Georgette Mosbacher is casting an acquisitive eye over British fashion group Laura Ashley Holdings Plc, Wednesday's edition of the Times newspaper said.

The Times quoted Mosbacher, the wife of former U.S. commerce secretary Bob Mosbacher, as saying, "I still very much like the company." She also said that it was "possible" she might make an offer for the firm.
Mosbacher approached Laura Ashley two years ago but was turned down by Sir Bernard Ashley, who refused to sell his shares in the group.
The Times said that Mosbacher's interest in the company stems from a belief that she could effect a turnaround along the lines of the one she performed at the La Prairie cosmetics company.

Laura Ashley issued its second profit warning in four months on Tuesday when it revealed that it would post a first-half pretax loss of 4.5 million pounds ($7.2 million), followed by a lower-than-expected second-half profit and break-even results for the year.
The company also said that it plans to cut back its U.S. expansion programme, opening only 13 stores this year and none next year due to losses there.
